# Independent review: SIZEBIASCOMP response

Reviewed raw SHA256:
`784e16445c64c1b480cfb0fdc5740182ad59253a775bfc8ab7dc0c44a654eafd`

## Verdict

**ACCEPT_FULL_FIELD_TRANSPORT_CONVERGENCE_AND_CUTOFF_RATE_OBSTRUCTION_ONLY.**

The half-density construction retains the physical weight, changing
conditional projection, cutoff, nonlinear likelihoods, and arbitrary finite
complex rows.  Equations (9)--(10) correctly recover the original `V` at the
terminal size-biased law.  The endpoint estimates give finite field and
first-derivative source constants for each fixed row; the projection
variation and score are not discarded.

The first-innovation calculation is correct.  Tilting the first `m` H
factors yields the `6^{-m}` crossing term, while the Lipschitz remainder is
`15^{-m}`; the constant in (28) follows from these two contributions.
The positive leading coefficient follows from the stated Markov bound and
strict positivity of `r`.  Equations (31)--(36) correctly retain the jump at
`t=1`, so the literal cutoff field cannot have a uniform `15^{-m}` MSE rate,
although its full MSE errors are summable.

The signed telescopes (37)--(44) are absolutely convergent and preserve the
micro/loss/projection identity at every level.  Equation (47) correctly
excludes only almost-sure nonnegative increments of this particular
coupling.  It does not establish a sign for the mean increment or for `V`.
The remaining bulk/trace balance (43) is genuinely unpaid.

Appendix A was independently replayed from an ephemeral copy: all 16 exact
rational checks passed.

bounded full weighted fields and moving projection derivatives
strictly positive leading cutoff crossing coefficient at rate 6^(-m), error O(15^(-m))
full MSE error sums and signed quadratic telescopes absolutely converge
literal cutoff field cannot retain the scalar 15^(-m) MSE rate for nonzero jump
pathwise nonnegative increments of this exact coupling are false
open: V nonnegativity on every finite row
counting: One bounded construction/repair package; no canonical counter reset or reconstruction, no Barvinok restart.
